properties.name: check_doc_versions' hermetic suite passed before, during and after its fact-reading function was replaced wholesale — it only ever exercised the claim-matching half, so a green suite said nothing about the half that changed
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-24. `tools/check_doc_versions.py` has two halves. `foundation_tag()` READS THE FACT every doc claim is measured against, out of the tree. `claims()` MATCHES prose against that fact. Its hermetic suite `tools/test_check_doc_versions.py` had three tests, all on the second half: the repo as it stands passes, a stale claim is caught, and rewording the prose fails loudly rather than disabling the check.

Increment 4 deleted the thing `foundation_tag()` read — the `dynograph-*` git-tag pin in the workspace `Cargo.toml` — so the gate went red, correctly, with `FAIL: could not find any dynograph-foundation tag pin`. The function was then REPLACED WHOLESALE: it now reads `^//! tag      vX.Y.Z` out of the provenance headers the absorption decision requires every absorbed module to carry, with new failure modes for no-header-anywhere and for modules naming different tags.

🛑 **THE SUITE PASSED 3/3 BEFORE THE REWRITE, AND 3/3 AFTER IT, AND NEVER ONCE TOUCHED THE FUNCTION.** `grep -n 'foundation_tag\|tag = "v\|provenance' tools/test_check_doc_versions.py` returned NOTHING. A green suite was reported for a rewritten function it did not reach, and the green was true and worthless in the same breath.

⭐ WHY THIS ONE IS WORTH KEEPING. The near-miss is not "a function was untested" — that is ordinary. It is that **the suite's green was read as evidence about the change**, in a session that had already been caught twice that day reading a narrow gate as a wide one. The check that caught it was not a tool: it was asking, before trusting the pass, WHICH LINES THE SUITE ACTUALLY EXECUTES. That is the same habit `rule:success-is-read-from-the-authoritative-object` names — the value you read is not the value you think you are reading — applied to a test suite rather than to an exit code.

CLOSED BY ADDING WHAT WAS MISSING, not by noting it: three tests now pin that the provenance headers are where the tag comes from, that losing every header FAILS rather than passing empty, and that modules absorbed from different vintages are caught — the successor to the old "five pins that drifted apart" check. Suite is 6/6. The two failure-mode tests mutate the real source files and restore them in a `finally`; restoration was verified by grep afterwards, because a test that corrupts provenance headers on a crash would be worse than the gap it closes.

⚠️ GENERALISES, AND IS NOT MEASURED BEYOND THIS ONE CASE: reflow2 has eleven python gates, most with a paired hermetic suite, and NOTHING checks whether a suite reaches the whole of the gate it guards. Whether the others have the same shape is unknown — stated as an open question, not as a finding.
